title: Plant and establish ornamental plants from containers into open ground

lessons.title: Getting ready to plant
lessons.html:
Getting ready to plant

Plants from the nursery come in containers like plastic bags, pots or seedling trays. When we plant them in the garden, we must do it well. A plant that is planted badly may die, even if it was healthy in the nursery.

Check the plants

  • Check the label. Is it the right plant for this place?
  • Look at the leaves. They should be green and healthy.
  • Look for pests like aphids or mealybugs. Do not plant sick plants.
  • Water the plants in their containers an hour or more before planting. A wet root ball comes out easily and does not fall apart.

Right plant, right place

Your team leader will show you where each plant goes. Some plants need full sun. Some need shade. Big shrubs and trees need lots of space. Do not plant trees close to walls, pipes or under power lines.

Before you dig

Ask your team leader if there are pipes, irrigation lines or electrical cables under the ground. Hitting a cable can kill you. Hitting a water pipe floods the garden.

Tools

  • Spade or garden fork
  • Trowel for small plants
  • Wheelbarrow
  • Compost
  • Watering can or hose
  • Knife or secateurs to cut bags
  • Stakes and soft ties for tall plants

Prepare the soil

Dig out weeds and stones. Loosen the soil with the fork. Mix in compost if your team leader says so. Good soil helps the new roots grow out quickly into the garden.

Wear gloves and safety boots when you dig. Lift heavy plants with your knees bent and your back straight.

lessons.title: Planting and looking after new plants
lessons.html:
Planting and looking after new plants

Digging the hole

  • Dig the hole about twice as wide as the container.
  • Make it about as deep as the container. The plant must sit at the same level as it was in the pot.
  • Loosen the soil at the bottom of the hole.
  • Fill the hole with water and let it drain if the soil is dry.

Planting steps

  1. Take the plant out of the container. Turn a pot upside down, hold the plant at the base between your fingers, and tap the pot. Cut plastic bags open with a knife; do not pull the plant out by the stem.
  2. Look at the roots. If they go round and round, gently loosen them with your fingers.
  3. Put the plant in the hole. The top of the root ball must be level with the soil around it.
  4. Fill in around the root ball with soil mixed with compost.
  5. Press the soil down gently with your hands or foot to remove air pockets.
  6. Make a small ring of soil around the plant to hold water.
  7. Water well, slowly, until the soil is wet deep down.
  8. Put mulch around the plant, but not against the stem.

Do not

  • Do not plant too deep. The stem will rot.
  • Do not plant too high. The roots will dry out.
  • Do not leave plastic bags in the hole.

Staking

Young trees may need a stake to hold them in wind. Put the stake in before you fill the hole, so you do not hurt the roots. Tie the tree loosely with a soft tie.

Aftercare

  • Water new plants often for the first weeks, until roots grow.
  • Check for wilting, pests and weeds.
  • Pick up empty containers and clean the area.

Key points

  • Water plants in containers before planting.
  • Ask about pipes and cables before digging.
  • Dig the hole twice as wide and as deep as the container.
  • Plant at the same level as in the pot; firm and water well.
  • Water new plants often until they are established.

quiz.question: How wide should the planting hole be?

options.text: About twice as wide as the container

quiz.question: At what level should the top of the root ball be?

options.text: Level with the soil around it

quiz.question: Why must you ask about pipes and cables before digging?

options.text: Hitting a cable can kill you and hitting a pipe floods the garden

quiz.question: What should you do if roots go round and round in the pot?

options.text: Gently loosen them with your fingers

quiz.question: When should a stake for a young tree be put in?
